sections.body: A FORCE is a push or a pull. Forces can start, stop or change the direction of things.
GRAVITY pulls things towards Earth. FRICTION slows things when surfaces rub. MAGNETS attract some metals, like iron.
SIMPLE MACHINES make work easier: levers, pulleys, ramps, wheels and axles.
Ice is slippery because there's very little friction. That's why we sprinkle grit or sand on icy paths.

quiz.q: Which force makes a dropped ball fall to the ground?
hints: Apples fall from trees because of it.
Friction slows things down; magnets attract iron. What pulls things down?

quiz.q: Why are trainers with rubber soles good for running?
options: They give more friction, so you don't slip
hints: Sand on an icy path stops slipping by adding friction. Rubber soles work the same way.
quiz.explain: Rubber soles grip the ground (more friction), so you don't slip.

quiz.q: Which object would a magnet attract?
hints: Plastic and wood are not metals.
Example: a magnet won't pick up a glass marble, because glass is not a metal.
quiz.explain: Magnets attract some metals, like iron. Plastic and wood are not attracted.
